stem.en: The mud volcano at Baratang Island bubbles mud, with no fire and no lava. What pushes the mud up?

text.en: Magma rising just under the mud

feedback.en: No. A mud volcano has no magma or lava.

text.en: Sea waves forcing water up into the caves below

feedback.en: No. The push comes from below the ground.

text.en: Rain water falling into the crater

feedback.en: No. The push comes from gas and pressure below the ground.
Yes. Gas and pressure push water and clay up.

explanation.en: At a mud volcano, natural underground gases and pressure push water and clay up through cracks. There is no molten rock, so it works in a different way from a fiery volcano.

hints.en: Is there any molten rock here?
What underground can push on wet clay?
